topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
target_audience: University students (computer science or general STEM background)

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
outline.target_audience: University students (computer science or general STEM background)

sections.title: The Intuition: Contextual Awareness
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'selective focus.' Explain that just as humans focus on specific words to understand a sentence, models must determine which parts of an input are relevant to others.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' the model must link 'it' to 'animal' rather than 'street'.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values
sections.content: Define the Q, K, and V vectors. Explain them via an analogy: Q (Query) is what I am looking for; K (Key) is what information is available; V (Value) is the actual content once a match is found.
sections.example: Like a library database: You type a search query (Q), the system matches it against book titles (K), and returns the actual page content (V) based on the relevance score.

sections.title: Visualizing Attention Scores (Dot-Product)
sections.content: Explain how relevance is calculated using the dot product between Q and K. Introduce the Softmax function as a 'weighting machine' that converts raw scores into percentages that sum to 100%.
sections.example: Visualized as a heat map matrix: High-relevance words glow bright gold, while irrelevant ones fade to dark blue, creating a 'focus spotlight' on the sentence.

sections.title: Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Whole Picture
sections.content: Explain why one 'spotlight' isn't enough. Multi-head attention allows the model to look at different parts of the data simultaneously—one head might focus on grammar, another on sentiment, another on entities.
sections.example: Like a team of detectives: Detective A focuses on who did it, Detective B focuses on where it happened, and Detective C focuses on when it happened. Together, they build a complete report.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Transformer Core
sections.content: Summarize how these weighted values (V) are combined to form a new, context-aware representation for each word, allowing the model to 'understand' complex relationships.
sections.example: A final animation showing a jumbled 'bag of words' entering the attention layer and emerging as a structured, meaningful sequence ready for text generation.

lecture_lines: Attention is all about selective focus.
Words need context to be understood.
The model tracks relations between words.

storyboard.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values
lecture_lines: We represent words as three vectors.
Queries find, Keys match, Values store.
This is like a library search.

Show Query vector mapping to Key space.
Highlight inner product result in #FF0000.
